newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-BOSRA SHAM IN DAZZLING ROYAL ASCOT DISPLAY.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-BOSRA SHAM IN DAZZLING ROYAL ASCOT DISPLAY.

text.p: Bosra Sham produced one of the most dazzling Royal Ascot displays for years on Tuesday, storming home by eight lengths in the Prince of Wales's Stakes for trainer Henry Cecil.
Winning jockey Kieren Fallon, 32, said: "She's a dream ride for any jockey, the sort that comes along once in a liftetime."

Winner of last year's 1,000 Guineas and Champion Stakes, Bosra Sham looks better than ever this season and ready to take on anything the rest of Europe or the United States has to offer. Taking up the running with 300 metres to go, Fallon stretched out effortlessly, leaving for dead the pacesetting Alhaarth, the mount of Frankie Dettori.
Alhaarth plugged on to be second, five lengths clear of London News, a former champion in South Africa and ridden by Doug Whyte.

Cecil, now with 61 Royal Ascot winners to his credit since his first in 1970, said of Bosra Sham:, the 4-11 favourite: "She is a great filly -- one of the best we have seen in a long time. As we're going to see her for the rest of the year let's try to appreciate her because we might not get another one like this for some time."
Next on the agenda is the Eclipse Stakes at Sandown in July followed possibly by the Sussex Stakes ar Goodwood.

The rest of the top action on the opening day belonged to Dettori who won the opening Queen Anne Stakes on 10-1 chance Allied Forces and followed up in the group one St James's Palace Stakes with an all-the-way success on Starborough (11-2).

Dettori, back at the course where he rode all seven winners in an afternoon last year, was at his inimitable best on Allied Forces, who provided a welcome winner for trainer Saeed bin Suroor and the Godolphin operation which has been badly out of form for much of the season.

Allied Forces took up the running with 200 metres to go and battled home by a ncek from the 11-1 chance Centre Stalls, the mount of Richard Quinn. with Ali Royal, the 9-4 favourite, ridden by Fallon, a further length and a quarter away.

Godolphin, the brainchilld of Sheikh Mohammed, has swept virtuallly all before it in the last two or three years only to fail this season. But Allied Forces signalled a clear change of fortune. "We have been in the wilderness for a long time," said Godolphin racing manager Simon Crisford."It's nice to be back in the winner's enclosure."
He added: "It's a huge relief to have a winner in the first race. I would hate to come here on the Friday looking for the last opportunity for a winner."

Starborough, Dettori's other big race winner, is owned by Sheikh Mohammed in his own right. The colt finished fourth in the English 2,000 Guineas but, improving all the time since, had behind him on Tuesday the winners of the Irish, French, German and Italian Guineas.
Dettori observed wrily: "I think Ascot is quite lucky for me."
